name: DBpedia
tagline: Wikipedia knowledge graph as structured Linked Data
description: DBpedia extracts structured data from Wikipedia and exposes it as a large public knowledge graph via SPARQL and Linked Data endpoints. Developers query entities, relationships, and multilingual facts (people, places, works, concepts) without scraping Wikipedia, using standard RDF/SPARQL tooling for research, entity linking, and semantic applications.

auth.details: Public SPARQL and Linked Data endpoints; no API key or OAuth required for standard use.

pricing.free_tier_limits: 10,000-row result cap; 120s query execution limit; 50 parallel connections/IP; 100 req/s/IP with initial burst of 120

rate_limits: 100 requests/second/IP with burst 120; 50 parallel connections/IP; 10,000 rows; 120-second query execution limit

example.request: curl -G 'https://dbpedia.org/sparql' --data-urlencode 'query=SELECT ?label WHERE { dbr:Berlin rdfs:label ?label . FILTER (lang(?label) = "en") } LIMIT 1' -H 'Accept: application/sparql-results+json'

use_cases: run SPARQL queries over Wikipedia-derived entities and relations
resolve a Wikipedia concept to a DBpedia URI and fetch RDF facts
look up multilingual labels and abstracts for a person, place, or work
entity-link free text mentions against the DBpedia knowledge graph
explore ontology types and properties for semantic data modeling
